programming_basics.title: Algorithms and programming
programming_basics.author: StudyPath project team
programming_basics.source: Original demonstration text; external readings are supplemental.

0.title: An ordered plan
0.body: An algorithm describes a finite sequence of steps for solving a defined problem. Start by identifying inputs, expected outputs, and a way to check whether the result is correct.

1.title: Try a small example
1.body: To calculate an average, add the observed values and divide their sum by the number of values. Before dividing, check that at least one value exists. This check prevents division by zero.

q1.prompt: What should be checked before dividing a sum by a count?

options.a: The count is greater than zero

options.b: A finite ordered sequence of steps

data_structures.title: Choosing a data structure
data_structures.author: StudyPath project team
data_structures.source: Original demonstration text; external readings are supplemental.

0.title: Organize values
0.body: A data structure organizes data so that a program can use it. Arrays provide indexed positions. A stack follows last in, first out. A queue follows first in, first out.

1.title: Match the operation
1.body: Choose a structure by the operations the program needs. A queue can represent a line of tasks waiting to be handled. A stack can represent a history in which the latest action is undone first.

q1.prompt: Which structure commonly processes the earliest arriving item first?

q2.prompt: Which structure follows last in, first out?

database_basics.title: Keys and related records
database_basics.author: StudyPath project team
database_basics.source: Original demonstration text; external readings are supplemental.

0.title: Identify a record
0.body: A relational database organizes records into tables. A primary key uniquely identifies a record within a table. Reusing a person's name as the only key can fail because different people may have the same name.

1.title: Connect records
1.body: A foreign key represents a relationship to a record in another table. A course record and a student's course attempt are distinct concepts: the course describes what is taught, while the attempt describes one student's participation.

q1.prompt: What uniquely identifies a record in a table?

q2.prompt: Why keep a course separate from a student's attempt?

options.b: They must always share every field
